target_customer: Physicians, starting with oncologists, plus pharma and research partners who pay to learn from physician expertise
problem: Doctors face clinical questions that guidelines and textbooks do not answer and are limited to their own closed network of colleagues. Mednet captures expert answers in a searchable physician-only network.
business_model: Free physician network funded by pharma and research partnerships, grants and sponsored services

founders.name: Samir Housri
founders.background_notes: About 20 years in digital media and technology startups per the YC page. Sibling of Nadine Housri.

founders.name: Dr. Nadine Housri
education: Clinical Research Training Program fellow, NIH
founders.background_notes: Radiation oncologist per YC page and TechCrunch.

investors: The Bonnie J. Addario Lung Cancer Foundation

competitors.name: Figure 1
competitors.what: Medical image sharing app for clinicians, named by TechCrunch as similar

competitors.name: UpToDate
competitors.what: Clinical decision support reference, named by TechCrunch as similar

competitors.name: Doximity
competitors.traction_then: 30,000 doctors registered in late 2011, about 40 percent of US physicians by 2014 per later coverage

technical_complexity.rationale: A Q&A and expert-routing network is standard web engineering. Verifying physicians and handling medical content adds operational effort.

defensibility.rationale: A verified physician network and accumulated expert answers are hard to copy, but general networks like Doximity could add Q&A.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source opened shows an incumbent copying or buying it. It remains independent and added AI answers and clinical trial search.

market_need_then: TechCrunch in 2017 said doctors rely on small closed networks for advice. The founders started it after their father's cancer treatment. By July 2017 more than 4,000 oncologists were on the platform, and the company said 25 percent of US oncologists had used it.

branding.name_origin: The name is a compound of medical and network, but no source states why it was chosen.
branding.brand_signature: Described by TechCrunch as a Quora for cancer

rebrands.why: Sources use both forms and no rebrand announcement was found.

branding.community_and_virality: STAT News and TechCrunch covered the launch. Partners include ASCO and ASTRO.

brand_strength.rationale: Name is generic and shares with other companies called Mednet, though press framing as a Quora for cancer gave it a memorable hook.

pivots.to: Multi-specialty network with Mednet AI answers
pivots.why: Company pages now describe AI plus literature plus physician expertise. Exact date not stated in sources opened.

outcome_analysis: Mednet launched out of YC in 2017 with an oncology Q&A network, raised a $1.3M seed in July 2017 and later won NSF and NCI funding. It grew to more than 40,000 physicians and added AI answers and trial search. No large later equity round was found, so growth looks capital-light and grant supported, with outcomes unclear.
notes: Seed amount is $1.3M in the body of TechCrunch although a social summary says $1.5M. NSF grant of $220K in February 2019 is from CB Insights only (unverified aggregator) and is recorded as a grant. Totals vary by aggregator ($1.3M to $2.7M). A $16.5M round reported by MobiHealthNews belongs to a different company, MedNet Solutions. The origin story page returned 403. Doximity source is from 2011, older than the batch, listed as an incumbent before founding.
